📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reports in Italy claim that Inter are interested in Arsenal centre-back Cristhian Mosquera, who has previously been linked with a move to San Siro, but pulling off a transfer for the Premier League winner in January will be a difficult task.

Inter, along with city rivals Milan, were among the clubs reported to be interested in Mosquera while he was still at Valencia, before joining Arsenal in the summer of 2025.

The Gunners paid a fee reported to be around €15m for the Colombia international, but after playing an vital role in Arsenal’s 2025-26 season, which ended with a Premier League title and a run to the Champions League final, reports from Calciomercato.com claim that he is now valued in the region of €40m.

Calciomercato adds that Inter are looking to rejuvenate their central defensive department in the near future and that they are interested in a potential deal for Mosquera, whose minutes have been limited following Arsenal’s signing of England international Ezri Konsa over the summer.

Mosquera has made five total appearances for Arsenal this season: Two in the Premier League, one in the Champions League, one in the EFL Cup and one in the Community Shield. He has not featured in the Premier League since August.

As per Calciomercato, Mosquera remains an ‘idea’ and a transfer in January will be difficult to pull off, but he is a player who remains of interest and could become a more viable option for the summer transfer window in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 06:47 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:49 EST, 26 November 2026.

The female reporter Jude Bellingham defended during an 'intimidating' post-match interview has praised the England star for being 'respectful' and 'well-mannered' as she opened up on the viral incident.

BBC Sport reporter Elizabeth Conway was speaking to Bellingham after Real Madrid's 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday when another journalist interrupted her as she posed a follow-up question, threatening to cut her interview short.

But the midfielder, 23, refused to answer the interferer and instead told him: 'Sorry, she's got one more [question].'.

Bellingham, who scored a sensational long-range goal on the hour mark to put Real Madrid ahead in the Champions League clash, was widely praised after footage of the incident went viral on social media, with fans applauding him as a 'class act' and 'role model for young men'.

Now Conway has added to the praise, stating the experience 'added a whole new layer to the love people have for Jude'.

Conway had been waiting to speak to the England star in the 'mixed zone' after the match – an area where journalists line up behind a barrier to interview players.

Jude Bellingham has won praise for his 'respectful' and 'classy' treatment of a female reporter.

BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had been interrupted by a male reporter when asking her second question, leading to Bellingham's intervention. Source: instagram/@elizabeth.conway_.

'It is utter carnage,' she told BBC Radio WM, opening up on the incident at the Bernabeu. 'Obviously as an English reporter at Real Madrid, getting Jude is exactly what we want, it's gold dust.

'Jude very rarely gives interviews, especially in the mixed zone. It is chaos... It's kind of every person out for themselves.

'You've got elbows, you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you.

'I'm one of very, very few female reporters and one of very, very few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so vital.'.

Conway admitted the mixed zone can be an 'intimidating' environment and being interrupted is unfortunately a routine part of being a post-match interviewer.

Admitting it was 'so nice' that Bellingham stepped in to stand up for her, she added: 'It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.'.

Conway, originally from Solihull, specialises in Spanish football and is based in Madrid, according to her Instagram, where she has more than 12,000 followers.

She had asked Bellingham in the mixed zone what had gone through his mind when he scored with his sensational effort at the Bernabeu.

According to recent reports, 'Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,' Bellingham remarked. 'I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.

In a recent development, 'It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it. It was a nice goal and crucial for the team being the second goal and gave us control.'.

The England superstar (right) had been in-demand after scoring with a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

After being interrupted and encouraged by Bellingham to pose her second question, Conway asked whether he feels like he is in the form of his life for club and country.

'My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter,' Bellingham added.

'Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.'.

Conway later shared the exchange on social media, writing: 'Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,' adding a handshake emoji while fans were quick to praise Bellingham for his 'classy' moment.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked his goal, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported the 23-year-old is in advanced talks over a new Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Bellingham has previously earned plaudits for his treatment of the media, having stopped to speak to a disabled reporter during the World Cup when several of his England team-mates had walked past, taking the time to answer his questions in Spanish.

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

“Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found issue had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

In a recent development, liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

Liverpool were meek, naïve, and while the Turkish side danced in the rain on the Asian side of the city, Iraola was left to dissect the most chastening 90 minutes of his short Anfield career.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s frustration because it’s a difficult place to come here and to play,” noted Iraola. “During most of the game, we were thinking: ‘OK we can win this one.’ But obviously it hasn’t happened. We conceded, I think, messy goals, especially the first and the third one. The second one is a rebound.”.

According to recent reports, yet it all started so smoothly. For all that Fenerbahce tried to put Liverpool out of their stride with a soundtrack of high-pitched whistling, Iraola’s side kept the ball well and they might have been ahead in the fifth minute but Victor Muñoz and Bradley Barcola, playing as a central striker, erred.

Liverpool have made the long trip to Turkey to take on Fenerbahce on matchday four of the Champions League.

Liverpool enter this fixture having won all three Champions League matches thus far, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal to make it nine points from nine for Andoni Iraola’s side. Liverpool’s five-game unbeaten streak was ended by Arsenal in the league on Sunday. They return to the city where the club enjoyed one of their most memorable nights, beating AC Milan in the Champions League final 21 years ago.

“Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool,” Iraola said. “It is difficult to find a more vital night. Tomorrow [tonight] it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight. In addition to the long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni, both Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have missed the trip to Turkey.

In a recent development, fenerbahce have made a slow start to their Champions League campaign, taking just two points from their opening three fixtures. They have drawn twice against Roma and Slavia Prague at home whilst they suffered a heavy 6-0 loss at Aston Villa. We have a very good plan, and we have to believe in this plan. No-one who loves Fenerbahce is happy with the current situation, but this is a huge opportunity. We have players who have won the Champions League and the World Cup.”.

They come into tonight’s match having lost back-to-back league games since drawing against Slavia Prague on matchday three of the Champions League. They have plenty of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Ederson, N’Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea star Cole Palmer has been the subject of criticism from ex-Blue Pat Nevin, who has admitted it’s getting harder to keep making excuses for him.

Palmer’s noticeable dip in form has been well-documented, with the England international not contributing nearly as much as he did in his first two seasons at Stamford Bridge.

Nevin has reluctantly admitted he’s concerned about Palmer, as enough time has passed now that the former Manchester City man can’t keep relying on excuses like coming back from an injury or playing in an unfamiliar role.

Speaking to Simon Phillips, Nevin expressed his concern about Palmer and attempted to explain what might have gone wrong for the 24-year-old.

According to recent reports, “There is a concern over Cole Palmer, I have to admit, though I hate admitting it. He was injured for large periods of last season, so he’s been going through injury recovery. You give him a slight pass for that.

“Then he was playing slightly out of position because Enzo Fernandez was in a central position, so you think that’s probably why he was peripheral.

Industry observers note that “But, can we stop this now? Can we actually say: ‘Cole, you’ve got to do it mate, it’s time now. It’s time to get back to that player that you were, controlling situations and doing genius things again.’.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Recent findings suggest that “It feels as if I’m always making excuses for Cole at the moment, but in the end, the numbers start telling you. Is he overthinking it? Because when Cole is at his very best, you can tell it’s completely off the cuff.

Industry observers note that “There’s something about young players when they come through, it’s a bit easier because you act on instinct. Sometimes that instinct goes because you overthink or because you’re over-coached.

“There are technical demands put on you like: ‘You must go to that part of the pitch.’ Well, wait a minute, maybe that’s not where I feel most dangerous in this game. I’d love to get inside the head of Cole Palmer, but it doesn’t look like an easy place to get inside, if I’m honest.

In a recent development, “Has he got the quality and skills to come back and be that player again? Yeah, of course he has. It’s a bit like Phil Foden, player of the year, amazing stuff, and then he had a complete period where he couldn’t score or create a great deal.

“It was hard to understand how that was even possible, but you can get it back. Phil’s doing well again now, and Cole can do it as well.

“The one thing I would underline is that it has nothing to do with being left out of the England squad. That’s absolutely not the case. Looking at Cole Palmer, there is no way he can blame England, Thomas Tuchel, or anything like that. Absolutely not.”.

It’s hard to know precisely what Palmer needs right now, but it’s been a generally chaotic period at Chelsea and that probably hasn’t helped him.

Palmer’s best form came under Mauricio Pochettino in his first season in west London, and since then he’s played under three different managers, not including caretaker or interim managers.

This is far from ideal for Palmer and many would argue he’s not the only one in this CFC squad struggling to perform at their best.

Newly introduced manager Xabi Alonso has not quite had the desired impact yet and that’s been an concern for a few players in this squad, such as Estevao Willian and pretty much the entire defence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Frank got off to a bad start as Crystal Palace manager against Coventry, but he has the chance to put it right on Thursday in the Europa League against Real Sociedad.

The La Liga outfit will travel to Selhurst Park for a European fixture, having won just one of their first four games in the competition, and they are desperate to get back to winning ways after a very slow start to the season.

Frank came into the club to replace Pierre Sage with the team sitting bottom of the Premier League and struggling to qualify for the knockout stages of the Europa League. But despite the team fighting back from losing positions twice in his first game in charge, he couldn't prevent the defeat.

One of the manager's biggest tasks is finding a way to stop leaking goals defensively, and a switch to a back four formation reveals that he is willing to implement his own ideas and style in as quickly as possible.

But he also needs to get more goals in the team, and he started off well with getting Jorgen Strand Larsen and Yeremy Pino on the scoresheet in the defeat to Coventry. The Norwegian striker has scored just nine times since joining the club from Wolves in a £50m deal back in the January transfer window, and the strike was just his fifth in the Premier League since his arrival.

With Ismaila Sarr, who was the team's top goalscorer last season, still sidelined for a number of weeks and seemingly not that keen to be at the club, Frank must find alternative solutions, starting with the game against Sociedad.

One player who the boss didn't have available to him for his Premier League debut was Jean-Philippe Mateta, but the Frenchman is ready and available to return in the Europa League.

Mateta was suspended after his red card against Tottenham, but that only stands in domestic fixtures. Now Frank has the chance to put the phenomenal forward into his starting lineup and find a way to get him firing again, trying to get the goals he can offer up into the side as promptly as possible.

Larsen was initially signed as Mateta's replacement before his move to AC Milan collapsed in January, but there is now an opportunity for the manager to try and pair them together and be a real handful for the opposition.

While Pino and Larsen scored at Coventry, Dwight McNeil was handed a surprise start and had a terrible outing, scoring the own goal that eventually saw them leave empty-handed.

According to recent reports, while McNeil and Mateta don't play in the same position, Frank has always been known for his tactical adaptability, and getting Mateta in the team is a no-brainer. He's fresh, strong, great in the box, and knows how to score goals. Alongside Larsen, they could form a formidable partnership, just like Ivan Toney and Bryan Mbeumo did at Brentford.

There are other attacking options in the side too, and if Frank wants to stick with his normal formation, then Larsen should be brutally axed despite his goal at the weekend because Mateta is by far the better player, and has proven it in the past.

Frank must unleash his best players to finally get back to winning ways and get off to a good start, while also helping the team in their chase to qualify in Europe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that long chains of sugars known as polysaccharides support many biological functions, from strengthening tissues to modulating cell signalling. Synthesizing these compounds in the laboratory with precise lengths and architectures, which are needed to establish how the structures of polysaccharides affect biological behaviour, has been difficult. Writing in Nature, Yin et al.1 now report an enzyme-based strategy that produces highly uniform polysaccharides and enables chains to restart growth after consuming all of the sugar building blocks in the reaction, once more sugars are added. The authors achieved this control by adjusting how readily an enzyme binds the small sugar molecules that are used to initiate the growth of each chain.

Alexander Isak believes he is moving in the right direction at Liverpool after delivering another outstanding performance in the Reds’ 3-0 Champions League victory over Club Brugge on Wednesday.

The Swedish international scored twice in Belgium, taking his tally to 10 goals across all competitions this season.

After an injury-disrupted debut campaign at Anfield following his British-record transfer from Newcastle United, the 27-year-old is increasingly showing why Liverpool invested so heavily in securing his services.

Speaking after Liverpool’s victory over Club Brugge, in comments shared by Fabrizio Romano, Isak was asked whether he was approaching his best form.

“It’s always difficult to say but I can definitely say I feel good, the team is in a good place, most importantly”.

“That’s where we want to be and hopefully it keeps getting better from here”.

Isak’s performances have also attracted praise from former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard.

Speaking on TNT Sports, Gerrard suggested opposition defenders would struggle to contain the Swedish international now that he has regained his fitness.

According to This Is Anfield, Isak has now scored in six consecutive away matches for Liverpool and has more than doubled his goalscoring tally from last season in just 18 appearances.

Perhaps the most encouraging aspect of Isak’s resurgence is his developing understanding with Florian Wirtz.

Both players endured difficult debut campaigns following their expensive moves to Anfield, but they are increasingly demonstrating their quality under Andoni Iraola.

Wirtz’s ability to identify spaces and deliver precise passes complements Isak’s intelligent movement and clinical finishing.

In a recent development, A fully fit and confident Isak gives Liverpool one of the most complete centre-forwards in European football. His influence extends beyond scoring goals, with his movement and technical ability creating opportunities for those around him.

Liverpool supporters have understandably been frustrated by the time it has taken their record signing to find consistency.

However, the patience shown towards him is beginning to pay off.

If Isak can maintain his fitness and continue developing his partnership with Wirtz, Liverpool could possess one of Europe’s most devastating attacking combinations.

The exciting part is that the Swedish international appears convinced there is still room for improvement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.

Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.

"Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp said, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves.".

Recent findings suggest that the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.

It paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

The 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.

Industry observers note that "I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp stated after the Netherlands match.

Recent findings suggest that "We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired.".

That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.

According to recent reports, but Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.

"They can both play, my goodness," said Klopp.

Scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

"A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still stated it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.

"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong.".

Proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he stated, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer.".

According to recent reports, while that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

In a recent development, "We've been through a tough time," he remarked. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it.".

Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.

"We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he said.

According to recent reports, in Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a disappointing start to the season, Tottenham Hotspur have the opportunity to make it five wins from six Premier League matches when they face lowly Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

Tottenham were bottom of the table after six league games and some pressure was beginning to build upon Roberto De Zerbi following a £300m-plus summer transfer spend.

However, their fortunes have turned ever since they beat Coventry City 3-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 19, and they now lie in 10th position and just six points adrift of the Champions League spots following Saturday's routine 2-0 home victory against Ipswich Town.

The win against the Tractor Boys was the latest sign of their improving home form, and they have now taken 10 points from a possible 18 on their own patch, but their away results need to improve if they want to seriously compete for a spot in the top four.

What is clear is that the Premier League chase for European football is wide open this season, with Manchester City and Chelsea dropping off in recent weeks, and Liverpool still showing a lack of consistency at times.

It means that Brighton and Hove Albion, Bournemouth and Brentford currently lie in the top six, and there is a significant opportunity for Tottenham too, if they can put a proper run together.

The north London outfit have only picked up one win on the road so far, scoring three times in five matches, with a goal difference of minus two.

De Zerbi will see a trip to 18th-place Sunderland as a major opportunity to record another three points, but he has some big selection decisions to make for the match.

The Italian coach left captain Micky van de Ven on the substitutes' bench against Ipswich following the international break, while Sandro Tonali was omitted because of illness and Mathys Tel missed out through injury.

The likes of Luca Williams-Barnett, Marcos Senesi and Conor Gallagher shone in the absence of those players, and now De Zerbi will be considering ruthlessly axing two of those on Wearside.

It's a positive for De Zerbi that he was able to give his captain a rest and that Tottenham could still deliver a comfortable three points against Ipswich, but it now means he has a bit of a dilemma.

Clearly, Van de Ven and his Dutch compatriot Jan Paul van Hecke are the first-choice and strongest partnership based on the early weeks of the campaign, boosted by the fact they also play together for the Netherlands.

But Senesi staked his own claim for the starting spot following an 8/10 performance against Gary O'Neil's side last weekend, where he looked both strong and assured alongside Van Hecke.

Perhaps what was most impressive about the Argentine was the ability he revealed in picking out passes into the midfield, which made a big difference to Spurs' attacking play.

Still, it will be difficult for De Zerbi to leave his captain out again, and you would expect Van de Ven to return to the XI in the north-east as the club look to sort out their away form.

Meanwhile, Gallagher was another who produced an 8/10 display alongside Mateus Fernandes in the heart of the midfield, impressing with his high work rate as usual.

It was an all-round performance from the Englishman though, who produced some vital blocks but was also good in possession, which isn't always one of his main strengths.

However, with £100m man Tonali likely to return following illness, you would expect him to walk straight back into the XI alongside Fernandes.

Gallagher can also play further forward too of course, but James Maddison's return to fitness and his display againt Ipswich surely mean he is another guaranteed starter at Sunderland.

De Zerbi would rather have these conundrums than not as it reveals the strength of the Spurs squad, but it also means he must make ruthless calls on a weekly basis.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FRESH YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune stated post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game strategy that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Newly introduced York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

Industry observers note that "We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins stated. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

Recent findings suggest that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness challenges over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

"I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill remarked. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

Sources indicate that in other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two vital blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of Newly introduced York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

Sources indicate that in the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas stated. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match plan that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

Industry observers note that the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

Sources indicate that "Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a proposal," Armas noted. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while presently headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

Sources indicate that "Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros remarked. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up strategy for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull Fresh York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce said. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

According to recent reports, the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

Industry observers note that "I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros noted. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

Industry observers note that "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

In a recent development, “Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”.

According to recent reports, those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United turned in a strong performance but were held to a 2-2 draw by Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday night, as Mauricio Pochettino continues to search for his first win as boss.

It has been revealed that the Red Devils conceded two penalties in two minutes in the first half, with Senne Lammens saving the first attempt before being beaten by Luis Suarez. Bruno Fernandes scored twice in the second half to give the side the lead, before Lammens committed a huge error by dropping a cross, which allowed Suarez to score a second.

United were aggrieved by the referee's performance after he controversially disallowed two goals and sent off Youri Tielemans late on, but the performance of the goalkeeper is what has largely grabbed the headlines.

The Belgian has struggled for form this season, with the club keeping just one clean sheet in all competitions, and fans have begun to question whether or not he should be keeping his place in the side for the upcoming game against Brentford.

Lisandro Martinez is another player who has received plenty of criticism this season for his performances, and he was involved in conceding a penalty against Sporting, although replays suggest it shouldn't have been given, while he also won the penalty that Fernandes converted to equalise.

Another player who has been criticised heavily is Diogo Dalot, and there are a number of players who fans believe shouldn't be in the side.

But one player who seems to continue to escape criticism is Mason Mount.

Industry observers note that the former England international joined the club from Chelsea in a deal worth an initial £55m back in 2023 but has managed just 8 goals in 84 appearances. Of those 84 appearances, only 35 have been starts, and he is yet to register a single assist in the Premier League or in European competition.

He also came on as a substitute in Pochettino's first game against Liverpool and immediately gave the ball away, which led to a goal, and he came on in the final moments against Sporting to do very little. Yet somehow, there is no mention of the fact he is still part of the squad.

With talks about the squad being rebuilt under Pochettino, and INEOS looking to trim the wage bill as usual, there should be no doubting that Mount should be on his way out of Old Trafford.

Representatives of Serbia's student-led movement were sworn in as lawmakers on Tuesday, just over four weeks after they ended Serbia's strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic's 14 years of rule.

The Students' List candidates officially took their seats in the inaugural parliamentary session as the first step for the youth-backed party toward forming Serbia's fresh government.

According to recent reports, the movement holds 140 seats in the 250-member parliament while Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) holds 103. The remaining seats belong to ethnic minority parties.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hundreds gathered outside the parliament building in the capital Belgrade, to show their support for the student-backed lawmakers, most of whom are teachers, professors and other professionals with little or no political experience.

Meanwhile, SNS candidates were met with a negative reaction from the crowd. A woman in the crowd poured yogurt over an SNS member's head as she climbed the steps to the parliament entrance.

According to recent reports, according to Serbian media, the newly elected lawmakers have been preparing for their first session for days. They will face veteran opposition politicians, including Aleksandar Vucic, who became the opposition leader after his defeat.

The Students' List will have 90 days to name a prime minister, present their programme and form a government, once the parliament is formed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the movement unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focused on making changes in domestic politics and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.

They pledged to improve healthcare, boost education and double the defense budget, along with many other reforms.

The election of a new parliamentary speaker will also lead to the appointment of a new acting president. The speaker has held the role since Vucic resigned in September to run for prime minister.

A snap presidential election must be called by November 27 and held by December 27.

Both parties are expected to put forward presidential candidates, but Vucic cannot seek another term because the constitution limits presidents to two terms in office.

Rare gene variants can affect a person’s height by up to 17 centimetres

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (756 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.
  • Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.
  • In a recent development, an analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.

Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.

In a recent development, an analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height. The work also uncovers previously unrecognized biological mechanisms that underly human growth.

The findings, published on 25 November in Nature1, might help with the development of treatments that mitigate height changes caused by some medical conditions, such as forms of dwarfism.

“The impact these genes have on any given individual can be massive in terms of accurately predicting their height or making sure they’re getting the right treatment for a disease,” notes Adam Locke, a statistical geneticist at the Regeneron Genetics Center in Tarrytown, New York.

In a recent development, about 80–90% of variation in adult height is caused by genetics. Projects analysing common gene variants have mapped thousands of DNA changes that can influence height. For example, a 2022 study identified more than 12,000 common genetic variants that collectively accounted for 40% of height variation in populations with European ancestry2.

However, how rare genetic variants (those found in less than 1% of a population) affect people’s height is less well studied.

Industry observers note that to systematically probe how rare variants contribute to people’s stature, Locke and his colleagues gathered DNA and height data. In total, they looked at sequencing data from more than 1.4 million adults. They analysed the protein-coding sections of DNA and ran a series of tests to spot non-random links between height and both common and rare gene variants.

Industry observers note that the analysis uncovered rare variants in 207 genes, which, on average, were linked to a height difference of about two centimetres. The team also identified 17 genes that had a particularly strong effect on height. The variants associated with this gene set all resulted in the production of non-functional proteins. In the study, over 700 people had at least one of these loss-of-function variants.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

According to recent reports, individuals carrying such a variant were, on average, about nine centimetres taller or shorter than were people who didn’t have that variant. The strongest effects included a 17-centimetre reduction in height associated with a change to the ACAN gene and an 11-centimetre increase linked to the FBN1 gene. These effect sizes are more than 50 times larger than those of most genes commonly associated with height.

“We would expect rare genetic variants that disrupt gene function to have larger effects than common genetic variants, but the magnitude of some of these effects is particularly striking,” claims Andrew Wood, a statistical geneticist at the University of Exeter, UK.

Anthony Gordon scored a brace for Barcelona in the Champions League against Sabah FK on Wednesday night, breaking a record set by Cristiano Ronaldo in the process.

The England international, who signed for the Spanish giants in the summer for £69.3 million, scored Hansi Flick's outfit's first two goals in Azerbaijan, setting them on their way to a 4-1 win. Fellow summer signings Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus netted the other two goals as La Blaugrana moved up to fourth in the Champions League table.

Eyebrows were raised when Barcelona opted to splash such a significant sum on Gordon in May, but he has largely silenced the sceptics so far with an encouraging start to life at the Camp Nou.

The wide man now has five goals and four assists to his name at his new club, and has subsequently established himself as a pivotal figure in Flick's team.

Not only is he producing fruitful numbers for the La Liga Champions, but he's also making history, eclipsing some of the best players of all time in some very specific metrics.

Gordon was renowned for his pace in England, but he's arguably developed a different side to his game since signing for Barcelona, and this was on show against Sabah.

Sources indicate that both of his goals demonstrated intelligence and awareness to be in the right place at the right time to tap home from close range. It's this smart movement that has seen him develop as a goal threat, and this has helped him set two newly introduced records.

Scoring four for Newcastle in Baku against Azerbaijani side Qarabag last season, Gordon's tally of six in the Eastern Asian nation set the record for the most goals scored by any English player in away games in one country in the Champions League.

These goals also made him the first player in history to score six away goals in a single country in the same calendar year in Europe's elite club competition.

He surpassed Cristiano Ronaldo, who netted five for Real Madrid in Turkey in 2013. Karim Benzema is at the moment joint second in this extremely niche statistic, also scoring five for Los Blancos, but in England in 2022.

Speaking after the match, Gordon stated that Azerbaijan must be his 'special place'.

"Even when we were 3-0 up, we didn't stop attacking," he remarked.

"We kept trying to score. That's our style, and I think it's very crucial. Baku must be a very special place for me... I should have scored another hat-trick tonight, but I wasted that chance with my left foot.".

The former Everton man even joked that he might need to move to Baku at some point in his life.

It has been revealed that "Maybe at some point in my life I need to move here! I've been very successful here, and yeah, great game today. Obviously two goals, so I'm happy, but potentially could have had a hat-trick, so still a lot of work to do," he told Stan (via Live Score).

Stonewallâs Rainbow Laces campaign, launched in 2013, became a fixture across English football, with players from all Premier League clubs wearing rainbow-coloured laces and captains donning rainbow armbands to promote acceptance and equality. The campaign aimed to support LGBTQ+ rights and foster inclusivity among fans and young people.

After over a decade of collaboration, the league will now lead its own campaign, timed to coincide with LGBTQ+ History Month in February, The Telegraph report.

"Rainbow Laces has benefited from a wide range of partners with a natural ebb and flow reflecting cultural and sporting changes," a Stonewall spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"Alongside other sporting bodies the FA has been instrumental in advancing LGBTQ+ inclusion at the grassroots level and more recently the Women's Super League has taken up the mantle as the women's game has grown - enabling Rainbow Laces to reach more diverse audiences.".

Despite Stonewall's efforts, recent reports from Kick It Out reveal an alarming increase in discriminatory incidents in football, including rises in sexism, transphobia and faith-based abuse, with racism continuing to be the most prevalent matter.

Controversies around playersâ attitudes to rainbow armbands have also made headlines. Last season, Ipswich captain Sam Morsy declined to wear one due to religious beliefs, while Crystal Palaceâs Marc GuÃ©hi faced criticism for personalising his armband with the phrase âI Love Jesus.â.

Additionally, Manchester United scrapped intends for LGBTQ+ support jackets after a player refused to participate.

With no openly gay or bisexual players currently in the Premier League, and the surge in discriminatory incidents, some question the timing of the split from Stonewall â an organisation highly respected for its work in LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Details of the Premier Leagueâs upcoming campaign are still under wraps, but as the league presses âreset,â thereâs hope it will introduce a meaningful and effective initiative that advances equality rather than undermines it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia on Tuesday mentioned it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month.

According to recent reports, since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the company's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.".

Nvidia is calling the upcoming group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

Recent findings suggest that the committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones mentioned in a statement.

The organization did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.

The decision was confirmed hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.

Sources indicate that "Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great organization," he said during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea.".

In a recent development, trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other big tech companies.

In a recent development, huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing firm.

In a recent development, that company, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three days after tearing up as he confirmed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino remarked he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

Recent findings suggest that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

According to recent reports, "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that says it's not important tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

According to recent reports, pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his prepares for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

"What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the fresh coaches that arrive here," Pochettino noted. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

It has been revealed that for all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

Recent findings suggest that for perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an vital new chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

Recent findings suggest that as for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his latest role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

According to recent reports, two years removed from starting a new job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-important clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

Industry observers note that "For me, it's not difficult," he noted of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most important [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

Wesley Fofana has apologised after angering Chelsea fans with his interview on French YouTube channel.

Fofana smashed his penalty over the bar against Liverpool in October but saw the funny side.

It has been revealed that the YouTuber who conducted the ill-timed interview hit back at the coverage in England of Fofana’s quotes. Regardless, Fofana has now seen fit to apologise to Chelsea, but it remains to be seen whether Alonso will stick with the Frenchman and Levi Colwill for Friday’s trip to Nottingham Forest.

Recent findings suggest that scoring goals is arguably the single most difficult thing to do in football. It's also the most vital thing to do in football - and that's why there's nothing quite as satisfying as when a player puts it all together and hits an incredibly rich vein of form. Watching someone tear teams apart and score week after week is a sight to behold.

Sources indicate that in the past, there have been some huge names embarking on this level of form in the Premier League. Some of the best strikers in the division's history have done so, and most recently, Erling Haaland became just the fourth player to put together two separate runs of seven games or more, doing so at the start of the 2026/27 campaign.

Haaland's run was ended by Brighton, but Bournemouth forward Evanilson has since scored in six straight league games, leaving him one away from joining the list.

Longest scoring streaks in Premier League history.

According to recent reports, kicking off our list, there are 11 players in Premier League history who have managed to score in seven straight games, with 13 runs between them. The most recent entry is Erling Haaland, who joined Mohamed Salah as the only players with two separate seven-game runs when he netted nine goals across seven matches early in 2026/27. The run began with a brace at Crystal Palace in August and ended with a towering header at Aston Villa in October, before Brighton kept him quiet.

His first seven-game streak came early in his Premier League career. The Norwegian's streak kicked off in just his third game in the division against Newcastle United, and the final goal of the run came at home to Southampton just under two months later.

Industry observers note that salah also did it twice for Liverpool. His first run came at the start of 2021/22, and he repeated the feat between October and December 2024, scoring twice in a 3-3 draw at Newcastle to make it seven straight during the club's title-winning season.

Taiwo Awoniyi hit form at the perfect time late in the 2022/23 season. His goals towards the end of the campaign played a significant role in Nottingham Forest avoiding relegation, and he continued the streak early into the next season.

Recent findings suggest that joe Willock is perhaps the most unlikely name on the list. On loan at Newcastle from Arsenal in 2020/21, the midfielder scored in each of his final seven appearances of the season. At 21, he became the youngest player to score in seven straight Premier League games and only the second Newcastle player to do so after Alan Shearer.

According to recent reports, more notable names to score in seven straight games include Shearer for Newcastle, Sergio Agüero for Manchester City and Thierry Henry for Arsenal. A surprising inclusion is Mark Stein for Chelsea back in the early 1990s. Shortly after joining the Blues from Stoke City in 1993, the forward went on an impressive streak, which was a Premier League record at the time. Overall, that first season at Stamford Bridge was mightily impressive, with 13 league goals and 14 in all competitions, and that was as good as things ever got.

Rounding out the players who scored in seven straight Premier League games, we have Romelu Lukaku during his time at Everton, and a couple of ex-Arsenal strikers in Ian Wright and Emmanuel Adebayor.

There are far fewer players who managed to extend their scoring streak past the seven-game mark. Only four players in Premier League history have managed to score in eight straight matches: Daniel Sturridge, Jamie Vardy, Ruud van Nistelrooy and most recently, Alexander Isak.

After struggling to earn consistent game time at Chelsea, Liverpool took a chance on Sturridge when they signed him in January 2013. It instantly paid off, as the forward scored in his first three appearances for the club. That was a sign of things to come, as later that year, he began his very impressive run of scoring in eight straight league games for the Reds.

Alongside Luis Suárez, that 2013-14 season saw Liverpool come dangerously close to winning their first-ever Premier League trophy, and while the Uruguayan is credited for a large part of that, it's notable to acknowledge the role that Sturridge played in their success that season. After all, scoring in eight straight league games is no easy feat. Unfortunately, injuries soon seized control of the Englishman's career, and he never again reached the height he did during that campaign.

It has been revealed that similarly to Sturridge, Van Nistelrooy scored in eight straight games during his debut campaign for a Premier League club. The Dutch striker joined Manchester United in the summer of 2001 and managed to record the feat later that year, starting in December 2001. The similarities stop there, though, as unlike Sturridge, Van Nistelrooy only got better afterwards and his record of scoring in eight straight games wasn't even the best run he went on at Old Trafford. Unlike those two, Vardy managed to score eight games in a row quite late into his Premier League career, doing so in 2019 — but, by this point, he had already solidified himself as a Premier League legend.

The most recent addition, Isak, hit the ground running at Newcastle following his arrival in 2022, but he took his form to a whole new level during the 2024/25 campaign. Starting in December, he scored for fun, and netted in eight consecutive league games with his strike against Wolverhampton Wanderers extending his impressive run. After winning the EFL Cup for the Magpies, he joined Liverpool in a British-record deal in September 2025.

After scoring in eight straight Premier League games, Van Nistelrooy wasn't finished yet. Just over a year after that first streak ended, the prolific Netherlands international started another in March 2003 and surpassed his previous best, scoring in 10 straight matches. It was a record-breaking run for the Manchester United forward and spanned across two different seasons.

It has been revealed that as the first player to reach double figures in consecutive games scored, the Dutchman's record stood for over a decade, and it's criminal just how underrated he's become in the years since he left England behind. There were few players quite as effective as he was in front of goal and his excellent record backs that up.

Unfortunately for Van Nistelrooy, a certain cult hero came along and beat his record in the middle of what would become an incredible fairytale the likes of which the Premier League had never seen before.

According to recent reports, leading the pack with the most consecutive games scored throughout the history of the Premier League is Leicester hero, Vardy. The striker's story is the stuff of fairytales, having come from non-league football to become one of the most explosive strikers in football at the time.

According to recent reports, his rise with the Foxes was incredible, and during that historic 2015-16 campaign, when they defied all odds and won the Premier League trophy, he was one of the club's most important players. Sure, Riyad Mahrez and N'Golo Kante were earning a lot of plaudits for their incredible performances that year, and rightfully so, but there's no denying that Leicester wouldn't have stood a chance of upsetting the apple cart and getting their hands on the league title if they didn't have Vardy scoring at the rate he was.

"It’s eleven, it’s heaven for Jamie Vardy! Hold the back page! Hold the front page! A Leicester player has smashed the record!" stated Martin Tyler, commentating on Vardy's goal vs Man United.

Industry observers note that his combination of blistering speed and pinpoint accuracy saw him tear teams apart throughout his entire Premier League tenure, but it was never quite as good as it was during that infamous campaign. With the run starting early in the season, it continued until November when Vardy broke the record, quite fittingly, by scoring against Van Nistelrooy's former team, Manchester United. More than a decade on, nobody has come within three games of it, and it's hard to imagine anyone will break the Englishman's record anytime soon.

  • The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.
  • The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.

The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.

The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.

It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation.

The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas.

As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers.

He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup.

Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup.".

Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court.

His parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament.

Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail.

After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate.
