📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Carlos Augusto and his agent have arrived at Inter headquarters to sign the improved contract until June 2031. ‘The objective was to recognise his latest status.’.

The versatile defender has been one of the most reliable figures in the squad, especially under Cristian Chivu, playing as part of the back three or in a more advanced role on the left as a wingback in place of Federico Dimarco.

He even found a knack for scoring big goals, netting four with three assists in just 14 competitive appearances so far this season.

However, he was still one of the lowest-paid figures in the squad, pocketing €2.2m per season plus performance-related bonuses.

According to various reports, the focus of the talks were to reflect those performances with an improved salary, which is now expected to start at €3.5m plus add-ons.

“That was the objective of the negotiations in the end, to recognise his latest status,” confirmed agent Beppe Riso as he walked into the club headquarters this afternoon for the signing.

The 27-year-old joined Inter from Monza in the summer of 2023, initially on loan with obligation to buy for a total of €15.25m.

#129720. The haunting Masters meltdown that changed Rory McIlroy's career

📅 03 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1611 w)

The haunting Masters meltdown that changed Rory McIlroy's career

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Editor’s Note:  This story was originally published in April 2023.
  • Slumped on his club, head buried in his arm, Rory McIlroy looked on the verge of tears.
  • The then-21-year-old had just watched his ball sink into the waters of Rae’s Creek at Augusta National and with it, his dream of winning The Masters, a dream that had looked so tantalizingly close mere hours earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  This story was originally published in April 2023.

Slumped on his club, head buried in his arm, Rory McIlroy looked on the verge of tears.

The then-21-year-old had just watched his ball sink into the waters of Rae’s Creek at Augusta National and with it, his dream of winning The Masters, a dream that had looked so tantalizingly close mere hours earlier.

As a four-time major winner and one of the most decorated names in the sport’s history, few players would turn down the chance to swap places with McIlroy heading into Augusta this week.

Yet on Sunday afternoon of April 10, 2011, not a golfer in the world would have wished to be in the Northern Irishman’s shoes.

A fresh-faced, mop-headed McIlroy had touched down in Georgia for the first major of the season with a reputation as the leading light of the next generation of stars.

An excellent 2010 had marked his best season since turning pro three years earlier, highlighted by a first PGA Tour win at the Quail Hollow Championship and a crucial contribution to Team Europe’s triumph at the Ryder Cup.

Yet despite a pair of impressive top-three finishes at the Open and PGA Championship respectively, a disappointing missed cut at The Masters – his first at a major – served as ominous foreshadowing.

McIlroy shot 74 and 77 to fall four strokes short of the cut line at seven-over par, a performance that concerned him enough to take a brief sabbatical from competition.

But one year on in 2011, any lingering Masters demons looked to have been exorcised as McIlroy flew round the Augusta fairways.

Having opened with a bogey-free seven-under 65 – the first time he had ever shot in the 60s at the major – McIlroy pulled ahead from Spanish first round co-leader Alvaro Quirós with a second round 69.

It sent him into the weekend holding a two-shot cushion over Australia’s Jason Day, with Tiger Woods a further stroke behind and back in the hunt for a 15th major after a surging second round 66.

According to recent reports, and yet the 21-year-old leader looked perfectly at ease with having a target on his back. Even after a tentative start to the third round, McIlroy rallied with three birdies across the closing six holes to stretch his lead to four strokes heading into Sunday.

The youngster was out on his own ahead of a bunched chasing pack comprising Day, Ángel Cabrera, K.J. Choi and Charl Schwartzel. After 54 holes, McIlroy had shot just three bogeys.

“It’s a great position to be in … I’m finally feeling comfortable on this golf course,” McIlroy told reporters.

It has been revealed that “I’m not getting ahead of myself, I know how leads can dwindle away very quickly. I have to go out there, not take anything for granted and go out and play as hard as I’ve played the last three days. If I can do that, hopefully things will go my way.

“We’ll see what happens tomorrow because four shots on this golf course isn’t that much.”.

The truth can hurt, and McIlroy was about to prove his assessment of Augusta to be true in the most excruciating way imaginable.

In a recent development, his fourth bogey of the week arrived immediately. Having admitted to expecting some nerves at the first tee, McIlroy sparked a booming opening drive down the fairway, only to miss his putt from five feet.

It has been revealed that three consecutive pars steadied the ship, but Schwartzel had the wind in his sails. A blistering birdie, par, eagle start had seen him draw level at the summit after his third hole.

A subsequent bogey from the South African slowed his charge, as McIlroy clung onto a one-shot lead at the turn from Schwartzel, Cabrera, Choi, and a rampaging Woods, who shot five birdies and an eagle across the front nine to send Augusta into a frenzy.

Despite his dwindling advantage and the raucous Tiger-mania din ahead of him, McIlroy had responded well to another bogey at the 5th hole, draining a brilliant 20-foot putt at the 7th to restore his lead.

The fist pump that followed marked the high-water point of McIlroy’s round, as a sliding start accelerated into full-blown free-fall at the par-four 10th hole.

His tee shot went careening into a tree, ricocheting to settle between the white cabins that separate the main course from the adjacent par-three course. It offered viewers a glimpse at a part of Augusta rarely seen on broadcast, followed by pictures of McIlroy anxiously peering out from behind a tree to track his follow-up shot.

Industry observers note that though his initial escape was successful, yet another collision with a tree and a two-putt on the green saw a stunned McIlroy eventually tap in for a triple bogey. Having led the field one hole and seven shots earlier, he arrived at the 11th tee in seventh.

It has been revealed that by the time his tee drive at the 13th plopped into the creek, all thoughts of who might be the recipient of the green jacket had long-since switched away from the anguished youngster. It had taken him seven putts to navigate the previous two greens, as a bogey and a double bogey dropped him to five-under – the score he had held after just 11 holes of the tournament.

Mercifully, the last five holes passed without major incident. A missed putt for birdie from five feet at the final hole summed up McIlroy’s day, though he was given a rousing reception as he left the green.

Mere minutes earlier, the same crowd had erupted as Schwartzel sunk his fourth consecutive birdie to seal his first major title. After starting the day four shots adrift of McIlroy, the South African finished 10 shots ahead of him, and two ahead of second-placed Australian duo Jason Day and Adam Scott.

McIlroy’s eight-over 80 marked the highest score of the round. Having headlined the leaderboard for most of the week, he finished tied-15th.

Tears would flow during a phone call with his parents the following morning, but at his press conference, McIlroy was upbeat.

“I’m very disappointed at the minute, and I’m sure I will be for the next few days, but I’ll get over it,” he said.

“I was leading this golf tournament with nine holes to go, and I just unraveled … It’s a Sunday at a major, what it can do.

Sources indicate that “This is my first experience at it, and hopefully the next time I’m in this position I’ll be able to handle it a little better. I didn’t handle it particularly well today obviously, but it was a character-building day … I’ll come out stronger for it.”.

Once again, McIlroy would be proven right.

Just eight weeks later in June, McIlroy rampaged to an eight-shot victory at the US Open. Records tumbled in his wake at Congressional, as he shot a tournament record 16-under 268 to become the youngest major winner since Tiger Woods at The Masters in 1997.

Industry observers note that the historic victory kickstarted a golden era for McIlroy. After coasting to another eight-shot win at the PGA Championship in 2012, McIlroy became only the third golfer since 1934 to win three majors by the age of 25 with triumph at the 2014 Open Championship.

Before the year was out, he would add his fourth major title with another PGA Championship win.

And much of it was owed to that fateful afternoon at Augusta. In an interview with the BBC in 2015, McIlroy dubbed it “the most crucial day” of his career.

“If I had not had the whole unravelling, if I had just made a couple of bogeys coming down the stretch and lost by one, I would not have learned as much.

In a recent development, “Luckily, it did not take me long to get into a position like that again when I was leading a major and I was able to get over the line quite comfortably. It was a huge learning curve for me and I needed it, and thankfully I have been able to move on to bigger and better things.

“Looking back on what happened in 2011, it doesn’t seem as bad when you have four majors on your mantelpiece.”.

McIlroy’s contentment came with a caveat: it would be “unthinkable” if he did not win The Masters in his career.

Yet as he prepares for his 15th appearance at Augusta National this week, a green jacket remains an elusive missing item from his wardrobe.

Despite seven top-10 finishes in his past 10 Masters outings, the trophy remains the only thing separating McIlroy from joining the ranks of golf immortals to have completed golf’s career grand slam of all four majors in the modern era: Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, and Tiger Woods.

Recent findings suggest that A runner-up finish to Scottie Scheffler last year marked McIlroy’s best finish at Augusta, yet arguably 2011 remains the closest he has ever been to victory. A slow start in 2022 meant McIlroy had begun Sunday’s deciding round 10 shots adrift of the American, who teed off for his final hole with a five-shot lead despite McIlroy’s brilliant 64 finish.

Rory McIlroy: I will win the Masters.

Sources indicate that at 33 years old, time is still on his side. Though 2022 extended his major drought to eight years, it featured arguably his best golf since that golden season in 2014.

And as McIlroy knows better than most, things can change promptly at Augusta National.

However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

While the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

Industry observers note that the Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

Recent findings suggest that in Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

Industry observers note that the parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an glitch in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

In the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

In a recent development, okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“You’re not famous any more,” was one of the many taunts from The Kop aimed at Manchester United as Liverpool romped to a 4-0 win against Maurico Pochettino’s newly introduced team.

It has been revealed that of course, the early dismissal of Leny Yoro helped the home side and hindered their relegation zone opponents, but it’s hard to think the result would have been much different if this had been 11 vs. 11 throughout.

Liverpool finished the match having missed six big chances.

Alexander Isak, who was highly impressive in the first half, especially, with his off-the-ball movement and defensive work seemingly improving under Andoni Iraola, had a goal-bound effort blocked by Harry Maguire before the break and blazed a good chance wide in the second half. On another day, the Swede would’ve bagged two.

Bradley Barcola, who is far from a clinical finisher, had several opportunities to score himself or assist another. His pace for the third goal demonstrates where his strengths are but his composure in front of goal is an area of weakness.

"Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more,” insisted Pochettino post-match.

Maybe he was right, because Liverpool were sensational going forward, their front four connecting superbly, with Florian Wirtz the chief orchestrator. The German is really finding form for Iraola’s side and created an incredible 10 chances in the game - five of them defined as significant chances.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That’s the most chances created by a single player in a Premier League game since 2015.

Then there was Rio Ngumoha, the teenager absolutely tormenting Diogo Dalot, and unsurprisingly, completing the most dribbles in the game and having the most touches in the opposition box.

Liverpool ended the game with 60 touches inside Manchester United’s box, 28 shots on goal, and an xG of 4.35 - which is vastly higher than recorded in the 7-0 mauling three years ago (2.91).

That this was the fifth time in five years that Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker had played a game between these sides and won by at least a three-goal margin underlines the chasm between the two north-west rivals.

Alisson has stood in the Liverpool goal for a 7-0, a 5-0, two 4-0s, and a 3-0 victory all since 2021. For Liverpool fans who sat through the nineties, and parts of the noughties, having their dreams shattered by Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United, this is an experience that heals many childhood traumas.

But, as much as the 1990s were a barren decade in Liverpool’s history, they were never as bad as this post-Ferguson United are.

In a recent development, in fact, Liverpool never lost to United by more than a two-goal margin throughout their worst decade in the modern era. A 4-0 reverse at Old Trafford in 2003 and a 3-0 in 2014 are the only two times United have beaten Liverpool by more than two goals since 1969.

According to recent reports, in the last 50 years, United’s top scorer in this fixture is Marcus Rashford with seven goals. In that same time, Mo Salah scored 16 and Steven Gerrard nine.

Liverpool weren’t great during the ‘90s and for parts of the ‘00s, but they were at least competitive, especially in these fixtures that mean so much to supporters. United once again crumbled against their main rival, the two teams that have won the league title the joint-most times in English football history.

Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more.

“Going down with the City,” was another chant from the Liverpool faithful, who enjoyed seeing Iraola give some Jurgen Klopp-like celebrations, albeit much less extravagant, post-match. “Always I enjoy the moment,” stated the Spaniard. “I think we owe them (the fans) because we have had much better results away and we want to solve this and want to give them a big win and more to celebrate.”This is a huge win for Iraola, whose Liverpool career has begun well but seen disappointing home results in his first five league games.

Sources indicate that with a big win over Man United now under his belt, the confidence is brimming. “I’m pretty sure things are going to be falling into place for the club,” stated a buoyed Virgil van Dijk. “It takes a bit of time, when you are upcoming at any profession or any place you work at you need a little bit of time.”.

Time is something United don’t have, with only one league win by late November and firmly in the relegation zone.

This game and the situation of both teams, each with latest managers but at different stages in their development, truly underlined how Liverpool have managed to avoid the post-Klopp era capitulation that United have been troubled by for the last 13 years.

One club had a successful manager oversee an era of dominance, the other is a successful club with multiple eras of dominance under different managers.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty.

According to recent reports, earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment. Twice-yearly injections of this game-changing medicine — originally developed by the firm Gilead Sciences in Foster City, California — have been shown to be more than 95% effective at preventing HIV acquisition1. At the same time, as Nature reports in a News feature, an HIV vaccine — that would ultimately be a more robust solution to preventing HIV — is closer than ever before.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

In a recent development, in 2024, Gilead signed licensing agreements with six pharmaceutical companies, allowing them to make and sell generic versions of lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries, subject to regulatory approval. The recent FDA approval brings access a step closer in these countries. The cost to consumers has been set at US$40 per year, fuelling hopes that the drug will help to bring the global HIV epidemic under control.

These welcome developments contrast with the situation of public funding for HIV research and treatment, which is reeling from deep and unconscionable cuts from the US government. Many of the researchers whom Nature spoke to for the News feature had been funded by a programme for preclinical HIV-vaccine research run by the US National Institutes of Health (NIH). But the agency ended the programme last year, forcing researchers to scale back their research and seek alternative funding. Whatever funding comes next is likely to be less stable and less predictable than the NIH funding. It’s imperative that the cuts be reversed — or upcoming government funding sources found.

The path to an HIV vaccine has been long and bumpy, with decades of high-profile and costly failures, but there is now light at the end of the tunnel. The latest strategy — known as germline targeting — is designed to trigger the production of rare, highly potent antibodies that can prevent infection with diverse HIV strains. The technique has shown encouraging results in animal models2–4 and in early trials in humans5. Researchers are more optimistic than they’ve been in years that an effective HIV vaccine could be on the horizon.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

Sources indicate that but in the meantime, antiretroviral drugs such as lenacapavir look poised to have a big impact on infection prevention. In Africa alone, newly introduced infections could be cut by around one-third if just 5% of adults most likely to acquire HIV received the drug, and by half if it was given to one-fifth of adults, according to the Gates Foundation’s Institute for Disease Modelling in Seattle, Washington.

According to recent reports, but lenacapavir alone is unlikely to bring the HIV epidemic fully under control. There are several reasons for this: first, it’s not always easy to determine who needs the drug most. Second, to be effective, the drug must be taken for most of someone’s life — or at least while they are sexually active. Third, even $40 a year is unaffordable for people on the very lowest incomes.

Until recently, the United States was the stand-out funder for antiretroviral drugs for people living with HIV in low-and middle-income countries. That stopped in January 2025, when the US administration suspended funding. Although it later restored a limited amount, the effects have been devastating. A survey published earlier this year found that some 1,700 facilities previously offering treatments to people living with HIV had closed as a result (see go.nature.com/4a7ftp4).

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Sources indicate that trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Such instability highlights the importance of vaccines. “The funding cuts that happened in the past couple of years have really made it even more obvious how fragile that system of reliance” on drug access is, indicates Penny Moore, a virologist at South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Disease in Johannesburg. And that fragility, as Rogier Sanders, an HIV-vaccine researcher at Amsterdam University Medical Centre, says, is why research into a vaccine remains a priority: “A vaccine makes you independent from access to drugs.”.

Industry observers note that but the US cuts have not only curtailed the preclinical vaccine programme, they have also forced the postponement and scaling back of an HIV vaccine trial in South Africa. They have also affected supporting research, such as surveillance efforts tracking HIV evolution in African countries, says Nairobi-based Vincent Muturi-Kioi, who is leading development of HIV vaccines at the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative in Fresh York City.

It has been revealed that success stories such as the repurposing of lenacapavir as a preventive treatment and progress in vaccine development show the importance of investment in health. It is imperative that HIV vaccine research and deployment continues to receive support, at the same time as rolling out lenacapavir as widely as possible.

It could take more than a decade to translate the encouraging results with germline targeting into an effective HIV vaccine, and the current strategy might encounter more hurdles.

Sources indicate that the world is closer than it has ever been to an effective HIV vaccine and has a drug capable of preventing infections. Now is the time for funders to ramp up investment, not cut it back.

Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.
  • The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season.
  • Sources indicate that "It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.

Sources indicate that "It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions.".

Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about  what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”.

Industry observers note that many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

At the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, stated Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination.".

To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio.

It has always been clear, remarked Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

According to recent reports, "In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he said of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”.

Industry observers note that in the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer said he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case.".

That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.

"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a new sponsorship, investment deals," he said.

According to recent reports, indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

In a recent development, fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

Elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took problem with the factory farming practices  of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

Union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a fresh shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate firm, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.

"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.

"We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy.".

Striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.

"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he remarked.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal.".

Additional reporting by: Emmie Eernisse.

It has been revealed that the hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will compete in the 2026 NWSL Championship, and both clubs have unfinished business. Kickoff is set for Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.

The Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and fell short against Gotham FC in 2025. Now the Spirit have another chance at lifting the trophy, with a little extra incentive to do so, as the NWSL Championship returns to Washington, D.C.

Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was confirmed back in June.

The Kansas City Current are equally motivated to win the NWSL Championship after falling short in last year's playoffs. The club went on a record-setting regular-season run in 2025 and won the 2025 NWSL Shield but was eliminated in the quarterfinals. This year, they stormed through the postseason to reach the final game, looking for even more hardware.

Just a few days ago, some of the biggest stars were named to the NWSL's Best XI first team. Trinity Rodman and Croix Bethune were both honored on Wednesday night, and Bethune also took home her second Midfielder of the Year award. Rodman and the Spirit are looking for another NWSL Championship to add to their 2021 title, and Bethune -- who was traded from the Spirit in February -- is chasing history with the Current, who are still on the hunt for their first.

Here's everything you need to know about the significant game:.

Date: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160.

The Washington Spirit's return to a third consecutive final came after a third-place finish in the regular season, in which the squad scored 43 goals and midseason arrivals quickly acclimated, proving a key difference. Now the club is back in the final for the fifth time in its history.

Head coach Adrian Gonzalez and his roster got off to a quick start in the playoffs and demolished the Portland Thorns 4-1 at home. Rodman scored twice, and new signings Melissa Bethi and Clara Luvanga also got on the scoresheet. The Spirit swiftly followed that up with a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Utah Royals, with goals by Sofia Cantore and Luvanga after the group conceded the opening goal just two minutes into the semifinal.

The Spirit's attacking trio of Rodman, Cantore and Luvanga is gelling at the right moment and looking dangerous in the postseason, with all three forwards on the scoresheet in the playoffs.

"[The dynamic has] been great. Me and Soph have been able to build this connection a little bit longer, but it didn't take Clara very long. It's been amazing to see her grow and not only get comfortable but, like, get confident as well," Rodman remarked of the relationship with her teammates.

Industry observers note that "I think playing at Audi [Field] obviously helps with that. But seeing her thrive, celebrate herself, has been really cool to see. But on top of that, the connection, I think, as a winger, you always want a center forward that you can work with and build off of and learn from. So it's been an amazing experience so far, and I'm hoping that we show that again on Saturday.".

Under first-year head coach Chris Armas, the group got off to a rocky start to the season but quickly clawed its way to a fourth-place finish on the league table and co-led the league in goals scored (54) this season. The group has rallied around last year's short playoff appearance as a motivator, with several players saying this year is "personal" and citing the resilience they've shown. During some stretches of the year, the roster had to navigate varying injuries or player absences due to international duty: Temwa Chawinga came back from an injury and then participated in Women's AFCON in August; Bethune recently returned from a hip injury; and Michelle Cooper managed a lingering leg knock.

"I'm feeling great. The vibes are good, which also helps. I think in some way, in some capacity, we're all tired. We played 30-plus games this year, but I think the vibes are so high that it doesn't even matter at this point. Like, we only have 90 minutes left in our season, so if we're crawling off that field, that's what we're gonna do," Cooper stated.

"I'm glad everyone didn't come back healthy just in time for playoffs. Like we've had a couple months, two to three months, where all of us are healthy, which is nice. The level is constantly there. Even if something were to happen, we trust our bench. We trust the players that we have below us as well, and to be able to build the last two months and come into playoffs where everyone's kind of firing at the right time is exactly what we needed," she remarked.

According to recent reports, the Spirit and the Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday at Audi Field. The winner will then compete for more silverware next summer in the 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup against the 2026 NWSL Shield holders, Gotham FC.

Published: 07:54 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:31 EST, 23 November 2026.

It has been revealed that early on in On the Road, somewhere between Chicago and Denver, Jack Kerouac described the journey his main character was taking and some of the trepidation that came with each new horizon. ‘I was halfway across America,’ he wrote, ‘at the dividing line between the East of my youth and the West of my future.’.

Late on Sunday afternoon, as winter’s grey light turned to darkness on Merseyside and a bitter wind blew in off the Irish Sea, Manchester United’s fresh boss, Mauricio Pochettino, freshly arrived from Cincinnati, Ohio, arms folded grimly and tightly across his chest, stood on the touchline at Anfield and realised the full extent of what he had just got himself into.

Sure, the United job was too major to turn down. However far the club has fallen, it still has that lure. It still has the name, even if the name is now just one of those building facades on a film set.

It has been revealed that there is the name and then there is the nothingness that is concealed beyond the name. There is the mismanaged, mistreated void that United has become.

Recent findings suggest that and now United need to find out which version of Pochettino they have purchased. Because he is at a dividing line, too. Do they have the Pochettino who blazed a trail across the football landscape with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs, although he did not win trophies at any of those destinations?

It has been revealed that or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation gradually became becalmed at Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA national team? They better hope they can restart something in him because this is the biggest and the hardest job Pochettino has ever had and it will take a Herculean effort just to survive.

Do Man United have the Mauricio Pochettino who blazed a trail with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs? Or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation has fluctuated since?

That is what this season is about now for these fallen, ruined giants. It is about survival. Nothing more. If Pochettino did not realise it before, he will have realised it during that calamitous 4-0 defeat at Anfield: United are in a relegation battle and anyone who denies that is deluding themselves.

According to recent reports, that is just pride talking. The remnants of what pride remains at United, anyway.

Industry observers note that maybe it hasn’t quite seemed real until now. Just like the prospect of Leicester City winning the Premier League didn’t start to feel real until around Christmas of 2015-16. United going down would be up there with Leicester winning the title in terms of seismic events in the modern English game. It’s time to start taking relegation seriously.

Sources indicate that if you take the blinkers off for just a second, if you banish the muscle memory that tells you United are too successful and too rich to get sucked down into the Championship, then you have to accept that all the ingredients are there for United to get relegated. Take that name away and what’s left?

What’s left is a team that last won a Premier League game on August 30. What’s left is a team that has won one game all season. What’s left is a team that has conceded 34 goals across all competitions, more than any other team in Europe's top five leagues. What’s left is a team that has eight points from its first 11 league games.

Recent findings suggest that just for context, the Spurs side that spent most of last season haunted by the prospect of relegation, had 18 points at this stage of that campaign. If you still think the rabble right now representing the club are too good to go down, I think you are deluding yourself.

Yes, United played more than 80 minutes of the game against Liverpool with 10 men and, yes, the decision to send off Leny Yoro for his challenge on Alexander Isak was harsh. But the dismissal was also a fig-leaf for Pochettino and United. It was convenient. It was a disguise for what lay beneath.

Sources indicate that maybe the sending off of Leny Yoro was harsh. But United brought it on themselves.

Industry observers note that matthijs de Ligt (right) was bullied by Alexander Isak at Anfield. Pochettino's decision to play the Dutchman was a terrible misjudgment.

Recent findings suggest that de Ligt’s first action was to watch a long ball from Ronald Araujo sail over his head, gazing at it with a mix of horror and wonder, as you might if you were watching the trajectory of an alien spaceship. Yoro was not quick enough to read De Ligt’s discomfort and so the horror ensued.

It was Pochettino’s first game and it is impossible to judge him yet but it is possible to say this was a bad start.

There were even a couple of worrying signs in his post-match press conference when the bonhomie and the relaxed demeanour that are among his great strengths deserted him.

In a recent development, when he was asked about United being in the relegation zone, he snapped that it was a ‘cheap’ question because he had only just arrived at the club. He mentioned he saw fight in his players, which few others had seen. He blamed everything on the sending off of Yoro, even though it was his selection of De Ligt that had led to it.

Recent findings suggest that A few alarm bells started to ring. Only faintly and only in the distance but they were ringing nonetheless. Pochettino has had big jobs before but he has never had a job as big as Manchester United where the scrutiny and the expectation and the judgment is relentless and unforgiving.

Pochettino has dealt with Daniel Levy at Spurs, which may not have been an easy relationship, but he has never dealt with a clown-show like the one that Jim Ratcliffe has put in place at Old Trafford.

According to recent reports, united is rotten. Everyone can see that. Off the pitch, the club is at war with its own fans. The club gives every impression of trying to move on its most loyal supporters so that it can replace them with tourists and day-trippers who will spend more on tickets and in the club superstore and at the food stands.

It has been revealed that ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace,’ that banner in the Stretford End said a few weeks ago, and that is how the fans feel. They are more loyal than United deserve but their patience with their owners ran out a long time ago. Pochettino has a disaffected fanbase to deal with as well.

Industry observers note that united is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight. It feels as if it is getting weaker and weaker and weaker. And when Brentford arrive at Old Trafford next week, they will smell blood. Every club that comes to Old Trafford now smells blood.

Industry observers note that harry Maguire looks dejected at full-time on Sunday. United is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight.

Still think they’re too good to go down? Who are they better than in this league? Hull City? United don’t have the spirit of Hull City. They don’t have the togetherness. They don’t have the pride.

Recent findings suggest that hull got battered by Brighton on Sunday afternoon and still won 2-0. United could never have done that. United have already lost to Hull and Brighton this season, too.

So, yes, United are in a relegation fight. They’re one off the bottom of the league in the last week of November. Of course, they’re in a relegation fight. It’s on their new boss to get them out of it.

If Pochettino is on the wrong side of the dividing line of his career, if the best part of his journey is behind him, United are in big, big trouble.

Mauricio Pochettino barely had his feet under the table at Old Trafford - or rather, Anfield - on Sunday, but there he was throwing a teamsheet curveball into one of the biggest fixtures in the Manchester United calendar.

Starting Matthijs de Ligt was bold, to say the least, given the Dutchman had been out injured for such an extended period.

From the first minute, he looked every bit like a player who'd missed a large chunk of the past 12 months. Sky Sports co-commentator Gary Neville likened De Ligt's rustiness to his own return from a year out injured, after which he noted he felt like he'd 'had six pints'.

According to recent reports, against a Liverpool side that presses relentlessly and isolates defenders, De Ligt looked heavy-legged from the first whistle. He was caught flat-footed on the turn, half a yard late to second balls, and spun humiliatingly by Alexander Isak in the immediate build-up to Leny Yoro's sending off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

According to recent reports, you don't need your coaching badges to know what happens when you throw a rusty centre-half into that kind of intensity. Which begs the obvious question: did Pochettino do it on purpose?

Rarely do football managers strut into press conference and declare, "Half of this squad isn't fit for purpose, go and buy me new players." Not if they want to keep the dressing room on side, anyway.

With January around the corner and United still languishing in the bottom three, putting an undercooked De Ligt straight into the firing line felt like a very public memo aimed at the directors' box.

Every time De Ligt was left scrambling back towards his own goal, the argument for serious squad surgery in January effectively made itself.

Across his spells at Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, Pochettino was never shy about subtly nudging club owners when he felt his squad lacked depth or physical conditioning, letting results and personnel headaches do the talking ahead of a transfer window.

It has been revealed that maybe that's giving him too much credit for dark arts, of course. Pochettino has always been obsessive about physical standards, and there's a world where he simply wanted to throw his biggest names into the deep end to see who actually has the stomach for a scrap. Although, when your backline is already patched together, picking a senior international - even one running on fumes - can look like the lesser of two evils.

Still, Pochettino has been around the block too many times to be naive about what Liverpool do to half-fit defenders. Whether it was calculated boardroom politicising or sheer necessity, chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox got an eyeful. There is much for them to think about ahead of January, because they cannot think that appointing the Argentine before dusting off their hands will suffice.

Industry observers note that WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized plan is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

Rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

According to recent reports, "I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she mentioned Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

Sources indicate that five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

In a recent development, "I'm so excited," she noted. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

Sources indicate that "She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan said, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

Industry observers note that "I am excited to go in every day," Morgan remarked. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

"We have these big red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan said. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

Sources indicate that "I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman said. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many upcoming players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

"Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone noted. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

Before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a fresh construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

"Obviously, it was incredibly crucial for us to keep Trinity in this league," she said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

In a recent development, "She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] Newly introduced York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

"She's fun, she's engaging," Stone said. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

Rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

Industry observers note that "Trin is a generational talent," Stone said. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".

  • The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.

The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.

The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

Yet, after the first two days of trading, Anthropic stock closed Friday more than 20% below its opening price at $87.80, suggesting the hype had run ahead of what investors were willing to pay.

Anthropic's public listing is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

2026 was meant to be the year Wall Street’s trillion-dollar bet on what US President Donald Trump calls superintelligence (SI) started paying off.

In the first half of the year, it did. Many AI stocks hit record highs as US hyperscalers like Google's Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft recorded bumper earnings.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The second half of 2026, however, has brought a lot more uncertainty.

While the stock of chipmaker Nvidia pushed even higher last month, many hyperscalers and chip or memory firms have seen erratic movements in their stock prices.

Then, after the Democrats won control of the United States Congress in the midterm elections earlier this month, technology stocks sold off again dramatically.

The Magnificent Seven — including Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla — lost more than $1 trillion in value in a single trading day.

In a further twist, the AI sector took another hit last week as Nvidia shares plunged nearly 10% over two days.

The sell-off followed revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman reportedly suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy.

Huang resigned from the chipmaker, sending Nvidia's shares lower still and prompting a campaign by current and former staffers, investors and other key figures in Silicon Valley to have him reinstated.

"Is this the best timing?" asked Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at the Canada-based Stock Trader Network, in an interview with DW last week.

Dick mentioned Anthropic's valuation depends on whether it can deliver on a forecast by Goldman Sachs of more than $600 billion in revenue by 2030.

"If you get to a company with $600 billion in revenue, [a] $1.3 trillion [valuation] doesn’t sound that bad," he told DW. "But when you’re talking about a company with right now $52 billion in revenue, it sounds like it’s overvalued.".

Other analysts, like Vivek Seth, chief executive officer of Shaires Holdings, are more bullish about the Claude maker's prospects.

Sources indicate that "Anthropic is a once-in-a-generation tech giant," Seth told Bloomberg last week, noting how it has grown rapidly and has strong institutional backing. "Its IPO will establish a market-clearing valuation as conditions stabilize.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Wall Street is growing increasingly cautious about the sheer size of the AI outlay, amid warnings that future earnings may not justify the huge spending.

In September, investment bank Goldman Sachs estimated that hyperscalers need around $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their spending, leaving a gap of roughly $230 billion.

Recent findings suggest that "We're not in Kansas anymore," Dick quipped, borrowing a line from the classic movie "The Wizard of Oz," which means times have changed. Now, he said, investors are telling companies: "Show me the money.".

Other analysts, however, think it's too soon to expect the AI bubble to burst, including Kit Rees, investment strategist at London-based wealth manager Quilter, who thinks the post-election rout was a "healthy correction.".

"We’re still in the very early innings of the AI build-out," Rees told DW. "There’s still a lot of excitement around this technology and investors will want to have a slice of the pie.".

In addition to the roughly $800 billion invested in capital expenditures this year, AI hyperscalers plan to spend a further $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

It has been revealed that with many investors already running for the hills, Rees isn’t convinced the AI bubble will burst in the way skeptics expect. She thinks they should watch for stronger signs that the AI trade is maturing.

This could be "a slowdown in AI-related revenues for companies, or signs of less demand or less appetite for financing companies’ AI intends, be it through debt or through equity offerings," Rees told DW.

Sources indicate that there are early signs that investors have less appetite for AI-related debt. Borrowing costs for AI infrastructure firms like CoreWeave and Oracle have soared recently. Even the cost of insuring Nvidia’s debt against default has risen 76% in a month, CNBC reported recently.

It has been revealed that "They [Oracle] have been spending, some people say, like drunken sailors," Dick told DW. "They’ve compromised their balance sheet to a point where the stock’s fallen 65% from the highs.".

According to recent reports, that has not stopped Oracle, along with Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet, from continuing to concern fresh AI bonds. Since the end of last month, the four AI giants have declared deals worth $67 billion.

Rees remarked another sign could be any latest regulations that make it harder to build out US data centers, due to pressure on local water and electricity supplies.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that in his upcoming book "AI Mania: Blather, Bluster, and the Bubble of All Bubbles," economist Gary Smith compares the AI boom with earlier frenzies around railways, automobiles, television and the internet. He warns of a "frightful crash" when the AI bubble eventually pops.

Sources indicate that when the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, the tech-heavy Nasdaq stock market index lost nearly 80% of its value. Yet, previous bubbles have often lasted far longer than expected, making the timing of any crash hard to predict.

Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at UK-based investment bank Panmure Liberum, believes a reckoning could happen as early as next year.

"My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement told Bloomberg last month.

Editor's note: This article was first published on November 13, 2026 and was updated on November 18, 19 and 20 to reflect the latest developments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Julián Álvarez created both of Atlético Madrid's first-half goals as the visitors ended Getafe's unbeaten home league record this season.
  • Both of Atlético’s first-half goals in this matchday 13 LaLiga fixture came inside the opening 30 minutes.
  • Álex Baena opened the scoring in the 10th minute with a low, powerful shot from outside the area.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Julián Álvarez created both of Atlético Madrid's first-half goals as the visitors ended Getafe's unbeaten home league record this season. Atlético now sit two points behind Real Madrid, while Getafe are left one point above the relegation zone before the midweek European games.

Both of Atlético’s first-half goals in this matchday 13 LaLiga fixture came inside the opening 30 minutes.

Álex Baena opened the scoring in the 10th minute with a low, powerful shot from outside the area. It was his sixth LaLiga goal of the season. Johnny Cardoso doubled the lead on 30 minutes when David Soria missed a punch at a corner. It was Cardoso’s first league goal for Atlético.

Getafe finished with ten men. VAR confirmed a penalty involving Alexander Sørloth in the 89th minute. Dakonam Ortega Djené was then sent off in the 90th minute, having been booked in the 71st. Álex Grimaldo converted the penalty in the second minute of stoppage time for his fifth goal of the league campaign. About 10,000 spectators watched the game, according to Telemadrid.

Sources indicate that the visitors had 68% of the ball and completed 652 accurate passes to Getafe’s 238. They took 20 shots to the hosts’ 11. Getafe’s goalkeeper made 7 saves, while Jan Oblak needed to make only 1.

It has been revealed that álvarez played 75 minutes and created 4 key passes. Baena was rated 8.2 and Cardoso 8.13. Diego Simeone was without Ademola Lookman, Marc Pubill and Cristian ‘Cuti’ Romero for the trip.

In a recent development, the win followed two straight defeats for Atlético, 1-2 against Barcelona and 0-2 against Bayern München. It also followed last season’s 0-1 Atlético win at the Coliseum on 23 November 2025.

Barcelona lead the table on 36 points, with Real Madrid second on 33.

According to recent reports, pepe Bordalás’s side went into the game having lost every away league match without scoring. They had conceded 14 goals on the road.

#FINAL | Derrota.@GetafeCF 0⃣-3⃣ @Atleti #GetafeAtleti pic.twitter.com/lCpJZ8dHws.

It has been revealed that — Getafe C.F. (@GetafeCF) November 22, 2026.

Sources indicate that getafe have lost their last three games in all competitions, against Brighton, Villarreal and Atlético. They sit 17th with 12 points and a goal difference of -13. Levante are 18th on 11 points and Elche 19th on 10, both with a game in hand. Getafe could fall into the relegation zone if Levante or Elche win their games on Monday, VAVEL España reported.

According to recent reports, atlético return to action on Wednesday 25 November against Viking at the Metropolitano. That game is matchday 5 of the Champions League league phase, and both sides have four points going into it. Getafe travel to FC Iberia 1999 in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday 26 November.
